newsitem.title: FRANCE: French SNCF rail chief seeks finance talks.
newsitem.headline: French SNCF rail chief seeks finance talks.

text.p: French SNCF railways chairman Louis Gallois expects to hold fresh talks with the Finance Ministry on the hugely indebted rail company's financial situation, but is keeping his game plan to himself for the moment.
He also plans to push ahead with a new industrial strategy despite a government decision to delay passage of a rail reform bill through parliament while it attempts to allay trade union disquiet.

Gallois, interviewed by Reuters, declined to say, however, whether he was looking for a debt relief effort from the state beyond an existing plan to take 125 billion francs of more than 200 billion in debts off SNCF hands.
"We will have the opportunity of further discussions with the state," Gallois said when pressed on the possibility of seeking additional debt help.
"I would prefer to keep the discussions between myself and the ministry and not get too explicit," Gallois said.
The delayed rail reform bill envisages creating a separate state holding company to take 125 billion francs of debt off the SNCF's hands and become owner of the rail infrastructure.

Unions, already worried by a European Commission "White Paper" which proposes liberalisation of rail networks in the European Union, see the bill as compounding the threat to the SNCF's public service mission.

French railworkers spearheaded a crippling public service strike for more than three weeks last year after the government revealed plans to do away with early pension rights for rail employees but those plans have now been scrapped.

Gallois said the delay, which the government wants to use to open consultations with unions and parliamentarians to clear up misunderstandings, was unfortunate but that he would push ahead in the meantime with an industrial strategy designed to win back market share and to get back to break-even at operational level.

"It (the delay) is a problem because it creates uncertainty but the delay will not be time lost if it helps to allay fears and make things clearer," said Gallois, who recently moved to the SNCF job from the top post at state-owned Aerospatiale.
Gallois reaffirmed his aim of getting back to break-even by 1999, especially by cutting the cost of SNCF purchasing by the order of around 10 percent.
The SNCF is expected to show a loss this year of about 12.5 billion francs.

"We can make considerable savings on purchasing," Gallois said. "I've set the target of saving two billion (francs) by 1998 on the company's buying costs, which amounts to about 10 percent of total purchasing costs."
"But the return to break-even...means the debt question has to be seriously addressed. The company cannot carry the burden of a debt beyond a certain level," he said, declining to elaborate.
"We are still carrying intrinsic costs, such as the public service and especially in the regional domain, which the state has left on the SNCF books ," said Gallois.
